payload.feature:
LANDING PR for #794: the deadline tests that flake in the host exact-coverage gate under load stop reading wall time where the engine or the broker has not yet acted. TEST-ONLY.

Operator rulings:
- 2026-09-26, the threat model: catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.
- Decision 0071 rulings 5 and 9: a gate fails closed on what it cannot read, and every check is shown to bite.

THE BRANCH: story-794-deadline-tests, rebased onto main baa5a08f by the controller (clean, re-signed), ends at 20d106a8. It has two commits:
- 506439a8 (was 0feda664), story run implement-story-794-flake-effect-36657947 (review residual LOW, no security residual).
  - The root cause the review confirmed: under load, ADMISSION ran past a 1-2 s timeout_seconds. dispatch.rs:93-101 admits within (began, timeout_seconds) before anything spawns, and refuse_admission (broker/admission.rs:427-440) journals a plain effect/failed, so the attempt retries. It was not a slow driver start.
  - The fix moves the four hanging effect_replay/agent_fallback seats onto the engine's 30 s startup bound, with one shared constant, tests/support/engine.rs HANG_DEADLINE_SECONDS = 30, lengthens the hang sleeps to 300 s, and makes failures print each event's payload.
  - Its LOW: HANG_DEADLINE_SECONDS is a test-side copy of brokkr-runtime's private STARTUP (broker.rs:100), and no test pins the two as equal.
  - Rulings it asks: (1) it also moves the file's fourth deadline test, a_driver_advertising_replay_on_the_wire_parks (2 s -> 30 s); (2) the raise is to the engine's startup bound rather than "wait for accept before the clock matters", which this engine cannot express because the attempt's clock starts at began; the cost is 2.28 s -> 30.2 s for the two modules.
- 20d106a8 (was ccc2c4a4), fix round fix-round-794b-for-story-794-thr-b240f108 (review CLEAN). broker::session::readiness::tests::bindings_looked_up_before_a_stalled_write_still_guard_the_closure_given_up_on had failed 2 of 4 host gates (readiness/tests.rs:917: Refused(Handoff) where Failed(Masking) was due). Its deadline and its cancellation are now read only once the store's lookup is SEEN: `probed`/`seen` read the control pipe's NONBLOCK flag, which the sender sets only in `sent`, after publishing its lookup. They are never read by the clock alone. The test reproduced the failure with a scratch 600 ms sleep, and passed 20 of 20 at --test-threads=96 under load 3.3 to 13.5. `plan_lived` is untouched.
- Host exact coverage was green on the fix round's head (before the rebase).

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Judge, on HEAD (the base is baa5a08f):
1. The rebase: the diff against main is exactly the four test files (readiness/tests.rs, effect_replay.rs, agent_fallback.rs, tests/support/engine.rs). #792 (merged) changed readiness/tests.rs's `plan_lived` ledger tuple to three elements. Confirm the readiness test compiles and passes on HEAD, and that nothing of #792's is reverted.
2. Each fixed test still proves what it exists to prove, with the same name and expected values. Re-run one removal control from each commit in a scratch edit, see the stated failure, and restore.
3. The readiness probe's premise holds on HEAD: the sender makes the control pipe non-blocking only after its lookup is published. Read readiness.rs `delivered` and `sent` on baa5a08f. If the premise is false anywhere, the probe could pass vacuously: say so.
4. The 506439a8 LOW (HANG_DEADLINE_SECONDS copies a private constant): judge whether a test can pin it to STARTUP without a production change. If not, carry it as LOW with its reason.
5. Scope: test files only. No production code, witness, contract, fixture or policy change, and no suppression added.
6. For the PR: name every ruling needed. Expected: the two above from 506439a8, plus that the branch also closes the readiness flake (b9, the broker's author, agreed it rides here, its ruling being the operator's). Name the related follow-ups: #782 (a separate story, queued), and the machine_proof hung_driver_is_killed_at_its_deadline advisory.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it.

For the implement phase only: if a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding, in the test files only, with an exact test and a recorded removal control. When a test fails, keep its whole failure text (no grep or tail on cargo test output), and quote the panic and cause lines in your notes. Then run, all clean:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked -- broker::session:: (timeout 590)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- effect_replay:: agent_fallback:: (timeout 590)
- typos --hidden
- quality/ratchet.sh files and clones
- git diff --check

Other work runs in parallel:
- decision 0065 slice two (the-forge-b9; NEVER message it, or any brokkr-wt-* seat) runs U8c in brokkr-runtime engine.rs, engine/broker.rs, engine/artifacts.rs and brokkr-protocol broker/ledger*, and keeps off readiness/tests.rs until this lands;
- #753 edits brokkr-core, brokkr-store, brokkr-view and brokkr-cli fleet/, tui*, ui*;
- #697 edits brokkr-runtime places/compose and brokkr-cli recipes/;
- #782 edits brokkr-cli broker/rpc/tests/delivery.rs.

If a fix is needed, commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run every command in the foreground: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.


members.adversarial:
Reviewed HEAD 20d106a8 against baa5a08f adversarially, read-only for tracked files. Sole finding LOW, decision 0071 ruling 5: crates/brokkr-cli/tests/support/engine.rs HANG_DEADLINE_SECONDS=30 copies crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/broker.rs private STARTUP=30 without an equality guard. A later STARTUP change leaves the test budget silently divergent: e.g. STARTUP=60 and admission lasting 31 s again exhausts the test's 30 s admission budget before spawn. The documented reason is test-only scope and the runtime constant's privacy. Privacy prevents direct access, but a test-only include_str! source guard can pin the single declaration, reject unreadable/changed syntax and compare seconds without changing production (source guards already exist, e.g. tests/brokkr_folder.rs builder_arms). Thus direct access is unavailable, a fail-closed test pin is feasible, and the current unpinned duplication remains LOW; no security residual or finding above LOW.
Scope/rebase: exactly readiness/tests.rs, effect_replay.rs, agent_fallback.rs and tests/support/engine.rs differ; no production, witness, contract, fixture, policy or suppression change. #792's plan_lived is byte-for-byte unchanged and retains (attempt, OsStr::new("plan"), None). Test names and expected outcomes are preserved, with deadline text parameterized for 30 s. On baa5a08f (production unchanged on HEAD), delivered calls send_environment; handoff.rs publishes found(bindings) before send(&frame), which reaches sent; sent first sets FIONBIO=true. probed resets the filled pipe to blocking before cloning its writer; clone shares flags. No alternate setter makes this specific probe succeed before publication. The 30 s probe bound may fail the test if lookup never occurs, but the exact assertions prevent a vacuous pass.
Validation on HEAD: targeted readiness test passes; final cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked -- broker::session:: passes 46/46; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- effect_replay:: agent_fallback:: passes 11/11 (30.17 s). cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check pass. Tracked status remains clean. Exact coverage was not run, per charter; host evidence supplied in the commission is pre-rebase, not a new HEAD result.
Ruling 9 removal controls used an isolated git-archive scratch copy only, with complete cargo failure output unfiltered. (1) Changing process::eof_outcome's timed-out outcome from Indeterminate to Failed compiled and failed effect_replay::a_deadline_kill_with_attempts_left_parks_after_one_attempt: panic at effect_replay.rs:81:5, assertion left == right failed, left: 3, right: 1; journal cause effect/failed error: 'attempt exceeded its 30s deadline and was killed; its process tree is gone, and what it did is unknown; stderr tail: '. (2) Restoring baa5a08f's readiness test and adding a 600 ms delay before published.begin reproduced panic at readiness/tests.rs:912:9: left ("0002", "deadline", (Err(Refused(Handoff)), ([], Some(Failed(Refused(Handoff))), None))); right ("0002", "deadline", (Err(Failed(Failed(Masking))), ([], None, Some(Lifecycle)))). Restoring HEAD's test with the same delay passes (3.02 s). Additionally removing lookup publication fails HEAD at :944:9 with Refused(Handoff) instead of Failed(Masking). All scratch mutated sources were restored and verified byte-for-byte against HEAD; final tests run from the original worktree.
PR rulings to name: extending the fourth deadline test a_driver_advertising_replay_on_the_wire_parks from 2 to 30 s; using the engine startup bound rather than waiting for acceptance (admission's began-based budget cannot express that), accepting the approximately 2.28 to 30.2 s module cost; including the readiness flake with b9's agreement under the operator's ruling. Cite 0071 rulings 5 and 9 and the 2026-09-26 realistic-misuse/fail-closed threat model. Related follow-ups: #782 is a separate queued story; machine_proof::hung_driver_is_killed_at_its_deadline remains an advisory. This review produces no PR, commit or fix; landing is one PR through decision 0051.

Increasing STARTUP can silently make these tests shorten admission again. A direct Rust import cannot reach it, but a test-only include_str! source-declaration pin can assert the unique STARTUP declaration matches the shared test constant and fail closed on an unrecognized declaration; no production visibility change is necessary.
